topic: Yield Curve Inversion and Recession Signals
objective: Explain why short-term rates above long-term rates have preceded most US recessions, and what it does not prove.

topic: Free Cash Flow vs Net Profit
objective: Show why accounting profit can look healthy while cash drains, and how to compute free cash flow.
A business is worth the present value of its future cash flows; see what the discount rate does.
Read P/E as the inverse of earnings yield and compare it with bond yields.
Know when enterprise-value multiples are more useful than P/E, especially for leveraged firms.

topic: Bond Duration and Interest Rate Risk
objective: Explain why bond prices fall when yields rise and how duration measures that sensitivity.
Distinguish fixed-cost leverage in operations from debt leverage and why both amplify outcomes.
Understand how borrowed money magnifies losses and how a margin call forces selling.
Read an option payoff diagram: premium, strike, breakeven and maximum loss for buyers.
Understand what implied volatility measures and how India VIX reflects expected market swings.

topic: Sharpe Ratio: Return per Unit of Risk
objective: Compare investments on risk-adjusted return and understand the ratio's limits.
Explain why owning many stocks is not diversification if they all fall together.
Recognize how the pain of losses drives panic selling and poor timing decisions.

topic: Real Returns After Tax and Inflation
objective: Calculate post-tax, post-inflation return on an Indian investment and why nominal returns mislead.
Trace how inventory, receivables and payables decide whether a business needs cash to grow.

topic: Return on Equity and DuPont Analysis
objective: Split ROE into margin, asset turnover and leverage to see where returns really come from.
Understand how the yield gap over government bonds prices default risk.
See how a call, a put, the stock and a bond must price together to rule out free money.
Understand how an option's price reacts to stock moves (delta) and to time decay (theta).
Explain how short sellers profit from falls, and the costs and unlimited-loss risk they carry.
Value a stock as the present value of expected dividends, and where the model breaks.
Judge whether a company earns more than its cost of capital, not just accounting profit.
Measure how much a stock moves with the market, and what beta cannot capture.

topic: Value at Risk (VaR) and Its Blind Spots
objective: Understand what VaR estimates and why it fails in extreme market crashes.

topic: Repo Rate, Reverse Repo and CRR
objective: Explain how the RBI's policy rates and reserve requirements steer liquidity and lending.
Understand that real rate equals nominal rate minus inflation, and why it drives asset prices.
See how central banks expand their balance sheets to push down long-term yields.
Explain how interest rate differences set currency forward rates and hedging costs.
Show how a 1 percent annual fee can cost lakhs over decades of compounding.
Understand what the spread costs you on every trade and why liquidity disappears in stress.
Learn how bet size, not just edge, determines long-run growth and why full Kelly is risky.
Understand the trade-off of selling upside for option premium, and its capped-gain profile.

topic: Active Funds vs Index Funds: Fee Math
objective: Compare the cost gap of active and index funds and why most active funds trail benchmarks after fees.
Explain the two opposing patterns in returns and why each works over different horizons.
Spot when reported profit is inflated by one-time write-offs or aggressive accounting choices.
Show why daily-reset leveraged products can lose value even when the index ends flat.
Explain why long-term bonds usually pay extra yield for the risk of holding them longer.
Understand how buybacks lift earnings per share without creating new value by themselves.
Read debt-to-GDP as a ratio of growth to borrowing, and why interest costs matter more than size.

topic: Fiscal Deficit vs Current Account Deficit
objective: Distinguish government overspending from a country's external imbalance and why both matter for the rupee.
Explain why a rate cut takes months to reach loans, prices and jobs.
Recognize why published fund returns overstate performance by ignoring funds that were shut down.
